(verified via same probe). critical_code_review_comments: Net Worth SSOT (index.tsx L5648-5688): canonicalTotalAssets sums exactly-once (manual cash + manual investments + manual other rows + linked cash + linked investments + linked real estate + linked vehicles + linked other assets) — NO aggregated category headers included, which was the root cause of the double-count bug per problem statement. canonicalTotalLiabilities = manualLiabilitiesTotal + linkedLiabilitiesTotal. publishedNetWorth is only set when both sides reconcile (`Math.abs(nextNet - (canonicalTotalAssets - canonicalTotalLiabilities)) <= 0.01`), preventing partial-load flashes. Both Home (L5757 `netWorth={netWorth}`) and NetWorth screen (L5795 `canonicalNetWorth={netWorth}`) receive the SAME value.

Available Cash for BUILD (index.tsx L5691-5695): App-level `totalRestricted = sum of active restrictedBuckets`, `availableCash = totalCash - totalRestricted`. Passed to both HomeScreen (L5757) and LegacyScreen (L5797) as a prop. Legacy `buildStartingCash` (L4113) uses this exact prop, with defensive fallback to `(totalCash - (totalRestricted||0))`.

perMonthSurplus (index.tsx L4105-4112): returns exactly `totalMonths` rows, first row source='actual', remaining source='estimate'. BUILD projection at L4114-4122 sums month-by-month (`surplusRows.reduce((sum,r) => sum + r.surplus, 0)`) rather than multiplying, per spec. Subtitle at L4348-4359 counts actual vs estimate correctly.

Custom date filter (index.tsx L2790, L2801-2828, L2669-2678, L2848): 6th 'Custom' chip added to the DATE RANGE row, gated <input type='date'> pair for web with testIDs `tx-custom-from` / `tx-custom-to`, TextInput fallback for native. Date parsing splits YYYY-MM-DD into Y/M/D locally (avoids UTC-shift bug that would push July 1 → June 30 for west-of-UTC users). Reset button (L2848) clears customFrom/customTo alongside dateRange/accountFilter.

Transfer heuristic (spec item C) — not directly tested at runtime (would require seeding Plaid-shaped tx descriptions) but the changed regex `/transfer\b|internal transfer|online transfer|account transfer|xfer\b/` matches spec, and every other ACH/deposit/payment/check falls through to sign-based classification. Code review only.
